different trust-policy role sets; single-principal self-approval is always blocking.\\\\n- Decrypt authority is a separate control plane from ingest attestations: sidecar decrypt principals must be distinct from ingest dual-control principals, and ingest approval does not imply decrypt permission.\\\\n- For sensitive-source scope, keep unredacted payloads outside git-backed repo storage and allow only redacted payloads plus non-linkable digest envelope metadata into `docs/skill-ops-wiki/raw/`; sensitive provenance/token details remain in restricted encrypted sidecar storage.\\\\n- Keep privacy-gate scope lane-specific: evaluate only sensitive-source ingestion/promotion evidence and return `not_applicable` only when deterministic dual corroboration records both trusted classifier `sensitivity_scope=non_sensitive` and independent non-sensitive corroboration from an immutable-trust-root-attested source-inventory snapshot; `sensitivity_scope=unknown` is blocking.\\\\n- Keep privacy-gate required-check semantics centralized in `privacy-required-check-normalization.yaml` (separate owner/scope from CI declaration mapping); `.harness/ci-required-checks.json` and `required-check-scope.yaml` remain declaration/mapping-only.\\\\n- P5 introduces required-check normalization precedence (after P4 declaration derivation): `derive scoped` -> `apply privacy-required-check-normalization` -> `severity mapping`; unknown contexts or conflicting rewrites are blocking.\\\\n- Require `sensitivity_scope` evidence to originate from trusted classifiers declared in `sensitivity-classification-policy.yaml`; unsigned/untrusted provenance is blocking.\\\\n- Bind each ingested sensitive-source evidence record to tenant/run/rotation-scoped source-inventory keyed-HMAC binding tokens and trusted provenance metadata before downstream lane evaluators consume it.\\\\n- Persist git-backed `privacy-gate-evidence.json` as a schema-validated non-linkable digest envelope (classification result, attestation refs, replay-safe pointers) so promotion decisions and closeout can replay outcomes deterministically without exposing linkable sensitive metadata.\\\\n- Persist sensitive provenance/token details in restricted encrypted sidecar storage outside git-backed artifacts; promotion checks require attested linkage between envelope and sidecar, and repo-only evidence is insufficient for sensitive-scope pass decisions.\\\\n- Sidecar security boundary is explicit and fail-closed: `privacy-sidecar-contract.yaml` defines permitted decrypt authorities (runtime service role + break-glass dual-approval role), key custody requirements (KMS-managed key alias and rotation policy), mandatory immutable audit events (encrypt/decrypt/link/retention-expiry), retention windows, and hard failure semantics (`sidecar_unavailable`, `sidecar_attestation_missing`, `decrypt_authority_denied`) that block persistence/promotion. Decrypt-time authorization is mandatory on every sidecar access; unauthorized or unverifiable decrypt attempts are denied before data release.\\\\n- Sidecar retention/revocation semantics are access-time and promotion-authoritative: expired retention windows, revoked attestations, or stale key-rotation evidence must trigger decrypt denial at read time and force re-attestation before promotion.\\\\n- Break-glass decrypt authority is incident-scoped and bounded: requires dual approval from distinct break-glass principals, explicit incident/ticket binding, fixed TTL, immutable audit evidence, and automatic revocation at expiry.\\\\n- Update operational docs to align ownership, escalation, and recovery expectations with implemented gate behavior.\\\\n- Introduce `privacy_rollout_mode` in two steps:\\\\n  1. `privacy_rollout_mode=observe` (record privacy violations and ownership metadata, and keep sensitive-source promotion blocked),\\\\n  2. `privacy_rollout_mode=enforce` (privacy violations block promotion).\\\\n- Persist privacy-rollout transitions through `set_runtime_rollout_state.py`; policy introduction and state mutation are owned in this phase, while P6 owns final pivot enforce cutover only.\\\\n- Keep rollback target explicit: `privacy_rollout_mode=enforce` can revert to `privacy_rollout_mode=observe` only when diagnostics remain intact and unresolved violations stay visible.\\\\n- Keep rollout axes operationally independent: privacy-rollout transitions do not mutate pivot-rollout state directly; promotion gating evaluates both axes together and blocks on any incompatible combination.\\\\n- P5 may end with `privacy_rollout_mode=observe` only for non-sensitive-scope runs proven by dual corroboration; for sensitive-scope runs, P5 exit requires `privacy_rollout_mode=enforce` plus a signed `observe -> enforce` transition record in canonical rollout-state history.\\\\n\\\\n**Patterns to follow:**\\\\n\\\\n- Existing fail-closed safety checks and metadata validation style in governance scripts.\\\\n\\\\n**Test scenarios:**\\\\n\\\\n- Sensitive-source ingestion without classification metadata blocks repo persistence and promotion.\\\\n- Classification-complete flow passes while preserving actionable diagnostics.\\\\n- Non-sensitive lane-scoped runs emit pass-equivalent required-check status only when dual corroboration evidence includes immutable-trust-root-attested source-inventory proof (with explicit `not_applicable` diagnostics) so required-check parity remains satisfiable without fail-open classification.\\\\n- Raw-plane ingest fails closed when trusted classifier and independent scan disagree, when second-owner approval is missing, or when sidecar linkage/decrypt-authority checks fail.\\\\n- Raw-plane ingest fails closed when required dual-control attestations are produced by the same principal identity.\\\\n\\\\n**Verification:**\\\\n\\\\n- Privacy contract is enforced by default and reflected in operational docs.\\\\n\\\\n**Verification oracles:**\\\\n\\\\n- Sensitive-source repo persistence and promotion both require classification/redaction evidence before ready state.\\\\n- Dedicated privacy gate remains lane-scoped and returns `not_applicable` only when dual corroboration evidence exists (`sensitivity_scope=non_sensitive` + immutable-trust-root-attested independent non-sensitive source-inventory corroboration); it cannot fail unrelated repo-validation paths.\\\\n- Canonical git-backed privacy evidence envelope (`privacy-gate-evidence.json`) is schema-valid and replayable for every evaluated sensitive-source decision, and required sidecar linkage proofs are present/attested for sensitive-scope evaluations.\\\\n- Privacy gate `not_applicable` outcomes map to pass-equivalent required-check status for non-sensitive scope only through schema-validated `privacy-required-check-normalization.yaml` rules and only when dual corroboration evidence is present.\\\\n- Required-check normalization precedence is deterministic in P5 (`derive scoped` -> `apply privacy normalization` -> `severity mapping`) and fails closed on unknown context or conflicting rewrite outcomes.\\\\n- Operational docs map ownership and escalation to implemented gate behavior with no conflicting guidance.\\\\n- Observe-to-enforce transition preserves deterministic privacy findings and does not downgrade unresolved violations to informational-only state.\\\\n- Observe mode still enforces fail-closed behavior for sensitive-source promotion and cannot be used to bypass privacy gating.\\\\n- Observe mode emits explicit deterministic result `blocked_sensitive_scope` for sensitive-source promotions; this state is mandatory until `privacy_rollout_mode=enforce` preconditions are satisfied.\\\\n- Unknown or absent sensitivity classification is always blocking for promotion.\\\\n- Privacy rollback from `enforce` cannot produce a promotion-ready state for sensitive-source runs unless privacy preconditions are re-satisfied.\\\\n- Classification provenance checks fail closed when evidence is self-attested or produced by a non-authorized classifier.\\\\n- Independent non-sensitive corroboration checks fail closed when source-inventory proof is mutable-repo-only and not anchored to immutable trust-root attestation.\\\\n- Sidecar boundary checks fail closed when decrypt authority is outside contract, key custody/rotation attestations are stale, required audit events are missing, or retention policy metadata is absent.\\\\n- Sidecar evidence reuse fails closed when retention is expired, attestation is revoked, or freshness constraints are not met; promotion requires fresh sidecar re-attestation.\\\\n- Break-glass decrypt use fails closed when incident binding, dual-approval provenance, TTL bounds, or automatic revocation evidence are missing.\\\\n- Classification/provenance records are bound to exact tenant/run/rotation-scoped source-inventory keyed-HMAC tokens for the evaluated promotion payload; cross-run stable token reuse is forbidden in git-backed artifacts.\\\\n- Raw evidence writer-boundary controls fail closed when any non-ingest process attempts to mutate `docs/skill-ops-wiki/raw/`.\\\\n- `validate_all.sh` restore/rollback manifest for P5 explicitly includes all P5-owned privacy/normalization assets and mutators (`Infrastructure/scripts/validate_wiki_privacy_gate.py`, `Infrastructure/scripts/validation-and-linting/verify_selection_gate_severity.py`, `Infrastructure/scripts/set_runtime_rollout_state.py`, `Infrastructure/scripts/verify_privacy_sidecar_contract.py`, `GOVERNANCE/runtime-separation/privacy-required-check-normalization.yaml`, `GOVERNANCE/runtime-separation/privacy-required-check-normalization.schema.json`, `GOVERNANCE/runtime-separation/privacy-gate-evidence.json`, `GOVERNANCE/runtime-separation/privacy-gate-evidence.schema.json`, `GOVERNANCE/runtime-separation/sensitivity-classification-policy.yaml`, `GOVERNANCE/runtime-separation/privacy-sidecar-contract.yaml`, `GOVERNANCE/runtime-separation/privacy-sidecar-contract.schema.json`, plus any P5-mutated required-check declaration/mapping surfaces) with rollback-integrity checks.\\\\n\\\\n**Failure stop conditions:**\\\\n\\\\n- Any path permits sensitive-source repo persistence or promotion without privacy gate evidence.\\\\n- Enforce-to-observe rollback hides unresolved privacy violations from closeout reporting.\\\\n- Any path permits `not_applicable` without dual corroboration (`sensitivity_scope=non_sensitive` + immutable-trust-root-attested independent non-sensitive source-inventory corroboration).\\\\n- Any path accepts untrusted classification provenance for `sensitivity_scope`.\\\\n- Any path accepts dual-control attestations from a single principal for sensitive-source ingest decisions.\\\\n- Any path treats expired or revoked sidecar evidence as promotion-authoritative.\\\\n\\\\n**Exit criteria:** AC8, plus sensitive-scope exit gate (`privacy_rollout_mode=enforce` with signed `observe -> enforce` transition history record); non-sensitive-scope runs may exit in `observe` only when dual-corroborated `not_applicable` evidence is present.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] **P6 / Unit 7: Enforce Activation Handoff and Final Gate Cutover**\\\\n\\\\n**Goal:** Perform a deterministic post-P5 handoff that activates `pivot_rollout_mode=enforce` only after privacy and closeout preconditions are fully satisfied.\\\\n\\\\n**Requirements:** R11-R13, R15, R17-R18\\\\n\\\\n**Dependencies:** P4, P5\\\\n\\\\n**Files:**\\\\n\\\\n- Modify: `Infrastructure/scripts/validate_all.sh`\\\\n- Modify: `Infrastructure/scripts/set_runtime_rollout_state.py` (state-transition writer already established in P0; P6 adds final handoff logic and rollback safeguards)\\\\n- Modify: `Infrastructure/scripts/runtime-separation/build_runtime_separation_current.py`\\\\n- Test: `tests/test_runtime_rollout_state_contract.py`\\\\n\\\\n**Approach:**\\\\n\\\\n- Treat P6 mode-handoff checks as implementation rollout controls only; normative delivery contract acceptance remains AC-based and spec-locked.\\\\n- Evaluate final activation preconditions after P5 completion:\\\\n  1. sensitive-scope precondition requires signed rollout-state history containing an authorized `privacy_rollout_mode: observe -> enforce` transition (with replay/concurrency checks satisfied),\\\\n  2. privacy gate activation-eligible outcome is either:\\\\n     - `enforce_pass` with `privacy_rollout_mode=enforce` when sensitive-source ingestion/promotion evidence is in scope,\\\\n     - `not_applicable` only when deterministic dual corroboration proves non-sensitive scope (`sensitivity_scope=non_sensitive` + immutable-trust-root-attested independent non-sensitive source-inventory corroboration),\\\\n  3. privacy gate non-activation hold state remains explicit:\\\\n     - `blocked_sensitive_scope` for sensitive-source scope while `privacy_rollout_mode=observe`,\\\\n  4. `pivot_rollout_mode=warn_visible` in canonical rollout-state artifact,\\\\n  5. no blocked lane obligations,\\\\n  6. drift gate passing,\\\\n  7. blocker metadata completeness and evidence redaction contracts passing,\\\\n  8. rollout-state artifact and closeout output report the same mode-state tuple,\\\\n  9. state-transition write authorization and artifact-provenance checks pass,\\\\n  10. lane-owner/freshness policy contracts are schema-valid and pass `verify_runtime_policy_contracts.py`,\\\\n  11. reader-compatibility gate passes for all independently versioned closeout surfaces (`current.json`, `CloseoutHealthSnapshot`, `closeout_health_reported`) with schema-valid `reader-compatibility.json`,\\\\n  12. live required-check parity evidence is passing and fresh for runtime-pivot-owned scoped checks (`required-check-enforcement.live.json`) using the explicit age rule (`evidence_age_hours <= required_check_live_parity_max_age_hours`, `now_utc <= fresh_until_utc`, and `fresh_until_utc` derived from `generated_at_utc` using `required_check_live_parity_max_age_hours` with bounded `required_check_live_parity_clock_skew_minutes` tolerance) validated by `Infrastructure/scripts/verify_required_check_enforcement.py --live` and rechecked by `Infrastructure/scripts/validate_all.sh`,\\\\n  13. rollout-state transition history contains one signed/attested live `shadow -> warn_visible` transition record produced by `set_runtime_rollout_state.py` with replay/concurrency checks satisfied.\\\\n- Apply one explicit handoff transition from `pivot_rollout_mode=warn_visible` to `pivot_rollout_mode=enforce`.\\\\n- Define the reverse transition contract for operator rollback (`pivot_rollout_mode=enforce` -> `pivot_rollout_mode=warn_visible`) with the same authorization, parity, and evidence-preservation checks.\\\\n- If any precondition fails, remain in `pivot_rollout_mode=warn_visible` and emit deterministic blocker diagnostics.\\\\n\\\\n**Verification oracles:**\\\\n\\\\n- `pivot_rollout_mode=enforce` becomes reachable only through this post-P5 activation handoff.\\\\n- Failed preconditions do not partially activate enforce mode.\\\\n- Privacy-mode transitions do not implicitly mutate pivot mode; incompatible tuples are handled by deterministic blocking decisions.\\\\n- Sensitive-source runs cannot activate `pivot_rollout_mode=enforce` while privacy gate outcome is `observe` or unresolved.\\\\n- Enforce activation fails closed when reader-compatibility records are missing/stale/incompatible for any independently versioned closeout surface.\\\\n- Enforce activation fails closed when live required-check parity evidence for runtime-pivot-owned scoped checks is missing, stale, or failing.\\\\n- Rollback from `pivot_rollout_mode=enforce` to `pivot_rollout_mode=warn_visible` preserves blocker evidence continuity and artifact parity across operator surfaces.\\\\n\\\\n**Failure stop conditions:**\\\\n\\\\n- Enforce activation occurs without all listed preconditions.\\\\n- Activation handoff can produce mixed mode state between artifacts and operator surfaces.\\\\n\\\\n**Exit criteria:** AC5, AC6, AC8\\\\n\\\\n## System-Wide Impact\\\\n\\\\n- **Interaction graph:** Runtime validators feed the current artifact builder; comparator and wrapper gates consume normalized outputs; `ask` surfaces expose the same decision envelope for operators.\\\\n- **Error propagation:** Lane-specific blocker codes propagate into comparator results, then into promotion decision and closeout reporting. Missing blocker metadata is itself blocking.\\\\n- **State lifecycle risks:** Partial rollout of artifact schema, comparator rules, or wrapper interpretations can create split-brain decisions; each phase must update producer and consumer contracts together.\\\\n- **API surface parity:** `ask repo validate` and `ask repo doctor-catalog --strict` remain operator-facing contract surfaces and must reflect the same blocker precedence semantics as script-level enforcement.\\\\n- **Integration coverage:** Cross-script behavior must be proven with integration tests in addition to unit coverage because correctness depends on handoff between validator, artifact, comparator, and reporting layers.\\\\n- **Operational feedback loop:** Closeout snapshots become the canonical anti-stall signal; compatibility findings remain visible in degraded mode but non-blocking unless mapped to normative exception entries.\\\\n\\\\n## Risks & Dependencies\\\\n\\\\n- Risk: comparator/reader drift if schema changes land without synchronized consumer updates.\\\\n  - Mitigation: pair producer/consumer changes in one phase and keep fixture coverage in the same PR scope.\\\\n  - Owner lane: runtime-separation owner.\\\\n- Risk: false blocking from freshness-state inference or missing freshness provenance.\\\\n  - Mitigation: enforce explicit freshness defaults and block unknown freshness deterministically with actionable diagnostics.\\\\n  - Owner lane: skill-family certification owner.\\\\n- Risk: compatibility noise over-blocks degraded mode.\\\\n  - Mitigation: block only on normative exception-registry matches and keep all non-matching compatibility findings degraded-visible.\\\\n  - Owner lane: ask-contract owner.\\\\n- Risk: partial adoption of fail-closed installation governance causes silent promotion escapes.\\\\n  - Mitigation: enforce skill-stack/inspector checks before promotion decision computation and test both success and failure envelopes.\\\\n  - Owner lane: repo-standards owner.\\\\n- Risk: closeout gate rollout introduces abrupt hard-stop behavior before shadow/warn evidence stabilizes.\\\\n  - Mitigation: require staged rollout (`pivot_rollout_mode=shadow -> pivot_rollout_mode=warn_visible -> pivot_rollout_mode=enforce`) with explicit promotion-readiness review between stages.\\\\n  - Owner lane: runtime-separation owner.\\\\n- Risk: mode-state split brain between canonical state artifact and reported closeout output.\\\\n  - Mitigation: single canonical `rollout-state.json` owner plus parity tests that fail on state divergence.\\\\n  - Owner lane: runtime-separation owner.\\\\n- Risk: rollback from enforce mode suppresses blocker visibility and creates false confidence.\\\\n  - Mitigation: rollback is valid only if blocker evidence continuity and schema parity remain intact in the target mode; promotion decisions block on incompatible pivot/privacy mode tuples without implicit cross-axis mutation.\\\\n  - Owner lane: repo-standards owner.\\\\n- Dependency: runtime-separation inventory and manifest contracts (`readers.yaml`, `path-consumers.yaml`, `slices.yaml`) remain authoritative.\\\\n- Dependency: existing `ask` wrappers remain canonical operator entrypoints and must not diverge from script-level enforcement outcomes.\\\\n- Dependency: `Infrastructure/scripts/validate_all.sh` is the canonical enforcement entrypoint; `verify-work.sh` and `ask` surfaces must delegate to or consume its outputs without independent gate semantics.\\\\n- Dependency: blocker owner-role taxonomy from the pivot spec remains stable while this plan executes.\\\\n\\\\n## Documentation / Operational Notes\\\\n\\\\n- Implementation must update operational docs only where contracts change; avoid duplicating policy logic across documents.\\\\n- Closeout reporting should keep one canonical artifact source and avoid parallel, conflicting status outputs.\\\\n- Operational runbooks should explicitly separate:\\\\n  - promotion blockers (hard stop),\\\\n  - compatibility findings in degraded visibility state (visible but non-blocking unless registry-matched),\\\\n  - informational diagnostics (non-gating).\\\\n- Operational runbooks should include rollout-state annotations for each gate family (`pivot_rollout_mode=shadow|warn_visible|enforce`, `privacy_rollout_mode=observe|enforce`) so operators can interpret promotion outcomes correctly.\\\\n- Closeout reporting runbooks must document mandatory evidence redaction and allowlist rules for sensitive fields.\\\\n- Recovery sequencing from spec must be retained in operational guidance:\\\\n  1. lane 1 freshness blockers,\\\\n  2. lane 2 parity blockers,\\\\n  3. lane 4 contract blockers,\\\\n  4. compatibility findings in degraded visibility exploration, intent, and implementation shape:\\\\n\\\\n1. Ground in the environment first. Discover repo facts, patterns, configs, and schemas before asking.\\\\n2. Ask only when the answer changes scope, architecture, sequencing, risk, or an assumption.\\\\n3. Treat discoverable facts and preferences differently.\\\\n4. Avoid mutation while planning. Planning may inspect, search, and run non-mutating checks, but implementation belongs elsewhere.\\\\n5. Keep `update_plan` separate from plan mode. It is a live checklist/progress tool, not the durable plan artifact.\\\\n6. Final plans should be complete replacement artifacts. Partial deltas are easy for downstream agents to misapply.\\\\n\\\\nCodex chat uses `<proposed_plan>` to render approved plan text and can offer \\\\\\\"implement this plan\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"clear context and implement\\\\\\\" actions. Harness Engineering should not require that wrapper inside saved plan files, but it should preserve the underlying behavior: clear handoff, complete artifact, and a fresh-context implementation option when context pressure is high.\\\\n\\\\n## HE Plan Shape\\\\n\\\\nA Harness Engineering plan is ready when another agent can implement it without making product or architecture decisions. It should include:\\\\n\\\\n- problem frame and scope boundary\\\\n- source traceability to Linear/spec/requirements/brainstorm/UI criteria\\\\n- stable unit IDs and stable acceptance IDs\\\\n- dependencies and blocker order\\\\n- repo-relative file paths\\\\n- test file paths and concrete scenarios\\\\n- validation outcomes, rollout notes, rollback notes, and residual risks\\\\n- Linear/spec/plan/PR evidence matrix for tracked work\\\\n\\\\nThe plan should not include copy-paste implementation code, exact shell choreography, commit commands, or RED/GREEN/REFACTOR micro-steps. It may include directional sketches, diagrams, or pseudocode when they help reviewers validate shape, but those must be explicitly non-prescriptive.\\\\n\\\\n## Source Resolution\\\\n\\\\nPrefer the strongest source in this order:\\\\n\\\\n1. Existing plan path or obvious current plan to resume.\\\\n2. Active Linear issue and related parent/child/blocking issue graph.\\\\n3. Requirements or brainstorm document with acceptance examples and scope boundaries.\\\\n4. Approved spec or UI spec.\\\\n5. Direct feature, bug, refactor, or improvement description.\\\\n\\\\nIf the source has unresolved product blockers, route back to `he-brainstorm` or `he-spec`. If the source has technical questions that planning can resolve through repo or docs research, resolve them during planning. If the answer depends on writing code, running changed behavior, or seeing test failures, record it as a deferred implementation note.\\\\n\\\\n## Depth And Research\\\\n\\\\nUse the smallest depth that protects delivery:\\\\n\\\\n- Lightweight: compact plan, low ambiguity, straight-line dependencies.\\\\n- Standard: normal feature/refactor/bug with meaningful decisions and validation.\\\\n- Deep: cross-cutting, risky, ambiguous, migration/security/privacy/payment/external API work, or work touching external contract surfaces.\\\\n\\\\nLocal research always comes first. External research is warranted for high-risk domains, third-party APIs, missing local patterns, current framework behavior, or unfamiliar territory. Skip external research when local patterns are strong, recent, and directly applicable.\\\\n\\\\nReclassify lightweight work to standard when it touches environment variables, public APIs, CLI flags, CI, shared types, or externally consumed docs.\\\\n\\\\n## Synthesis And Assumptions\\\\n\\\\nUse Stated, Inferred, and Out-of-scope checkpoints when the agent has made consequential assumptions. In interactive work, revise and re-present after user changes until explicitly confirmed. In headless work, put unconfirmed Inferred bets in `## Assumptions` so reviewers and `he-work` can scrutinize them.\\\\n\\\\n## Deepening\\\\n\\\\nDeepen only where confidence gaps are real. Score sections by missing rationale, weak source grounding, vague units, bad sequencing, shallow tests, hidden blockers, weak rollout, and missing system impact. Dispatch targeted reviewers only for the section/risk being strengthened.\\\\n\\\\nDeepening should make the plan stronger, not longer.\\\\n\\\\n## Testing Guidance\\\\n\\\\nPlans must require real behavior tests. Avoid test scenarios that only assert mocks, snapshots of mocked children, or implementation internals. Include happy path, edge case, error path, and integration scenarios only where they genuinely apply.\\\\n\\\\nFor non-feature units, use an explicit no-test rationale rather than leaving tests blank.\\\\n\\\\n## Visual Guidance\\\\n\\\\nUse visuals when they reduce reader work:\\\\n\\\\n- dependency graph for non-linear unit dependencies\\\\n- interaction diagram for three or more affected surfaces\\\\n- comparison table for modes, variants, or alternatives\\\\n- state diagram for state-heavy lifecycle\\\\n\\\\nSkip visuals that duplicate prose or smuggle implementation detail into the plan.\\\\n\\\\n## Handoff\\\\n\\\\nAfter the plan is complete, hand off to:\\\\n\\\\n- `he-work` for implementation\\\\n- Linear workflow when creating or updating tracked work\\\\n- `he-deepen-plan` or document review when confidence gaps remain\\\\n\\\\nDo not auto-implement from `he-plan`. sequencing, blocker classification, and closeout verification\\\\n\\\\n- Added an explicit artifact-ownership matrix so `ce-work` can land the builder and harness changes without re-deciding where round metadata belongs.\\\\n- Tightened the deferred implementation questions with phase-one decision rules instead of leaving both as open-ended execution judgment.\\\\n- Strengthened validation and blocker-control gates so compatibility regressions, runner noise, and partial-rollout drift are classified consistently before closeout.\\\\n\\\\n## Overview\\\\n\\\\nUpgrade the skill-authoring family from a clean routing split into a coherent, evidence-backed authoring loop without undoing the lifecycle boundaries that were just stabilized.\\\\n\\\\nThis plan implements the approved spec by:\\\\n- making `skill-creator` produce a durable creator-to-builder handoff artifact for non-trivial skills;\\\\n- teaching `skill-builder` one explicit comparative iteration loop with frozen inputs, baseline rules, round states, and visible review evidence;\\\\n- keeping `skill-installer` and `plugin-builder` as downstream-only owners gated by `ContractValidityEvidence`;\\\\n- extending existing repo-native eval and reporting surfaces instead of introducing a new standalone viewer or parallel harness.\\\\n\\\\nPlan mode: `standard-plan`  \\\\nPlan depth: `deep`  \\\\nExecution posture: artifact-contract-first, then builder evidence surfaces, then eval enforcement, then downstream gating and full-family validation.\\\\n\\\\n## Problem Frame\\\\n\\\\nThe family routing contract is now clear, but the authoring loop still relies too much on implied escalation and loosely bundled evidence:\\\\n- `skill-creator` stops at starter drafting plus `quick_validate.py`, but does not yet leave behind one canonical durable artifact for the next stage;\\\\n- `skill-builder` already owns eval and description-optimization surfaces, but it does not yet present one first-class round model that explains how candidate and baseline runs are prepared, compared, reviewed, and promoted;\\\\n- downstream surfaces already point back to `skill-builder`, but they do not yet depend on one explicit evidence bundle and readiness-state story;\\\\n- existing report artifacts such as `result.json`, `summary.json`, `scorecard.json`, and `release_manifest.json` are useful, but they do not yet expose the specific comparative loop concepts the spec now requires.\\\\n\\\\nWithout a deliberate implementation sequence, execution will drift in one of two ways:\\\\n- the docs will describe the right lifecycle, but helper outputs and eval artifacts will still not prove it; or\\\\n- the harness will grow new fields and files ad hoc, but the family skills will still not teach the same contract to users and maintainers.\\\\n\\\\n## Requirements Trace\\\\n\\\\n- R1. Preserve the current family split and routing ownership across `skill-creator`, `skill-builder`, `skill-installer`, and `plugin-builder`.\\\\n  Trace: spec goals 1 and 7; `SA1`\\\\n- R2. Non-trivial creator-stage work must end with a durable dedicated handoff artifact file carrying the required context fields.\\\\n  Trace: spec `HandoffPackage`; spec invariants; `SA2`, `SA2a`, `SA3`\\\\n- R3. `skill-builder` must expose one explicit non-trivial iteration loop with prompt preparation, baseline selection, frozen comparison inputs, evidence capture, tuning assessment, and round decision.\\\\n  Trace: spec `IterationRound`, `ComparisonInputs`, `IterationRoundState`; `SA4`, `SA5`, `SA7`, `SA14`, `SA15`\\\\n- R4. Comparative evidence must preserve both machine-readable and human-reviewable signals, including metric unavailability and readiness-state distinctions.\\\\n  Trace: spec `EvalEvidenceBundle`; failure model; observability; `SA6`, `SA17`\\\\n- R5. Install and plugin packaging surfaces must remain downstream-only and require `ContractValidityEvidence`.\\\\n  Trace: spec downstream handoff rules; `SA9`, `SA10`, `SA18`\\\\n- R6. The implementation must stay repo-native by extending existing docs, eval manifests, and report artifacts instead of introducing a new viewer or cloned upstream workspace.\\\\n  Trace: spec goals 8 and non-goals; `SA11`, `SA12`, `SA13`\\\\n\\\\n## Scope Boundaries\\\\n\\\\nIn scope:\\\\n- authoring-family skill docs and metadata:\\\\n  - `Skills/skill-creator/`\\\\n  - `Skills/skill-builder/`\\\\n  - `Skills/skill-installer/`\\\\n  - `Skills/plugin-builder/`\\\\n- creator-stage artifact guidance and reusable template support\\\\n- `skill-builder` iteration, evidence, and reporting contract\\\\n- eval harness additions required to protect the new loop\\\\n- downstream handoff wording and readiness gating\\\\n- repo validation and sync work needed to keep public skill surfaces aligned\\\\n\\\\nOut of scope:\\\\n- merging or renaming the family\\\\n- a repo-wide skill-evals platform redesign\\\\n- a new dedicated UI artifact or UI plan\\\\n- a new standalone viewer application for eval review\\\\n- policy changes that would make `skill-builder` explicit-only\\\\n- runtime router changes outside the named family surfaces and existing eval/reporting helpers\\\\n\\\\n## Context and Research\\\\n\\\\n### Relevant Code and Patterns\\\\n\\\\n- `Docs/specs/2026-04-03-feat-skill-authoring-family-contract-spec.md`\\\\n  - likely home for the explicit round model if `SKILL.md` needs slimmer routing-level guidance\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/description-optimization.md`\\\\n  - existing route/description improvement guidance that can become one named step in the new round\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/evals.yaml`\\\\n  - current regression suite already covering routing and packaging boundaries\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/scripts/run_skill_evals.py`\\\\n  - current machine-readable report surface writing `result.json`, `summary.json`, `scorecard.json`, `release_manifest.json`, and `junit.xml`\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/scripts/test_run_skill_evals.py`\\\\n  - current downstream plugin-packaging boundary and validator expectations\\\\n\\\\n### Institutional Learnings\\\\n\\\\n- Keep local packaging canonical while importing useful upstream improvements; do not let the Anthropic reference reopen local family-boundary churn.\\\\n- This repo works best when the contract is visible in both markdown and the validator or report outputs that maintainers actually use.\\\\n- For repo-focused closeout, the standard broad validation path remains preflight first and `bash Infrastructure/scripts/validation-and-linting/verify-work.sh` before completion claims.\\\\n\\\\n### External References\\\\n\\\\n- Anthropic pinned `skill-creator` at commit `98669c11ca63e9c81c11501e1437e5c47b556621`\\\\n- OpenAI and Codex guidance already incorporated into the governing spec as of 2026-04-04\\\\n\\\\n## Key Technical Decisions\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 1: Use a dedicated target-skill artifact file at `Infrastructure/references/handoff-package.md` as the phase-one `HandoffPackage` path.\\\\n  - Rationale: it is durable, repo-visible, naturally colocated with the authored skill, and distinct from chat-only summaries or repo-global plan docs.\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 2: Reuse existing machine-readable eval outputs and add only one small human-review surface when necessary.\\\\n  - Rationale: `result.json`, `summary.json`, `scorecard.json`, and `release_manifest.json` already exist. The lowest-churn upgrade is to enrich them with round-state and baseline metadata, and add `comparison_review.md` only for the qualitative side the current artifacts do not express clearly enough.\\\\n  - Phase-one ownership map:\\\\n    - `result.json`: per-case candidate-versus-baseline evidence, round state, metric availability state, and optional qualitative-review artifact pointer\\\\n    - `summary.json`: run-level rollup of readiness decisions, blocked rounds, and neutral-baseline justification references\\\\n    - `scorecard.json`: CI-facing normalized pass/fail surface that stays additive and does not become the canonical narrative record\\\\n    - `release_manifest.json`: thin release-facing snapshot that references richer report artifacts rather than duplicating every round-detail field\\\\n    - `comparison_review.md`: optional run-scoped human-readable comparison artifact under the reports directory, not a versioned skill artifact\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 3: Keep `neutral_repo_baseline` planner-approved and human-justified only.\\\\n  - Rationale: allowing the builder lane to improvise baselines would weaken the whole comparative loop.\\\\n  - Phase-one source of truth: store the human approval and justification in `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/evals.yaml`, and require run artifacts to copy or reference that record rather than inventing a parallel approval surface.\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 4: Require route and description assessment in every non-trivial round, but require edits only when the evidence shows weakness or ambiguity.\\\\n  - Rationale: this keeps the loop disciplined without forcing meaningless churn into every pass.\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 5: Treat skill-sync and catalog regeneration as part of closeout when user-facing skill descriptions or metadata change.\\\\n  - Rationale: the family is public-facing, and stale indexes would make the new contract partially invisible even if the files themselves are correct.\\\\n\\\\n## Open Questions\\\\n\\\\n### Resolved During Planning\\\\n\\\\n- What should the smallest durable creator-to-builder artifact be?\\\\n  - Resolution: `Infrastructure/references/handoff-package.md` inside the target skill.\\\\n\\\\n- Which repo-native artifact should carry comparative review evidence?\\\\n  - Resolution: enrich the existing JSON report surfaces first; add `comparison_review.md` per run only for the human-readable qualitative delta that current JSON artifacts do not already express.\\\\n\\\\n- Should route and description optimization be mandatory every round?\\\\n  - Resolution: assessment is mandatory every non-trivial round; edits are mandatory only when evidence shows trigger weakness, ambiguity, or misleading descriptions.\\\\n\\\\n### Deferred to Implementation\\\\n\\\\n- Whether `Skills/skill-creator/Infrastructure/scripts/init_skill.py` should auto-scaffold a starter `Infrastructure/references/handoff-package.md` placeholder, or whether a reference template plus `SKILL.md` guidance is sufficient for phase one.\\\\n  - Deferred because the lower-churn path should be chosen after the execution pass confirms whether deterministic scaffolding materially reduces drift.\\\\n  - Phase-one decision rule: keep this docs-and-template only unless execution shows repeated artifact omission, validator ambiguity, or enough repeated manual drift that the template is no longer a reliable contract.\\\\n\\\\n- Whether `release_manifest.json` should duplicate all new readiness-state fields, or only reference the richer `summary.json` and per-case `result.json` outputs.\\\\n  - Deferred because the existing consumers may only need a narrow additive change.\\\\n  - Phase-one decision rule: keep `release_manifest.json` thin by default and only duplicate new readiness fields when a real consumer proves the pointer-plus-summary model is insufficient.\\\\n\\\\n## High-Level Technical Design\\\\n\\\\n> This is directional planning guidance, not implementation code.\\\\n\\\\n```mermaid\\\\nflowchart LR\\\\n  A[\\\\\\\"skill-creator starter authoring\\\\\\\"] --> B[\\\\\\\"target skill Infrastructure/references/handoff-package.md\\\\\\\"]\\\\n  B --> C[\\\\\\\"skill-builder round preparation\\\\\\\"]\\\\n  C --> D[\\\\\\\"candidate and baseline runs\\\\\\\"]\\\\n  D --> E[\\\\\\\"result.json and summary.json enrichment\\\\\\\"]\\\\n  D --> F[\\\\\\\"comparison_review.md if qualitative delta needs human surface\\\\\\\"]\\\\n  E --> G[\\\\\\\"ContractValidityEvidence\\\\\\\"]\\\\n  F --> G\\\\n  G --> H[\\\\\\\"skill-installer handoff\\\\\\\"]\\\\n  G --> I[\\\\\\\"plugin-builder handoff\\\\\\\"]\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nDesign notes:\\\\n- The creator-stage durable artifact should live with the target skill, not with the authoring-family skill itself.\\\\n- The builder loop should prefer additive artifact enrichment over a fresh storage model.\\\\n- Downstream surfaces should consume readiness evidence, not recreate or reinterpret it independently.\\\\n\\\\n## Implementation Units\\\\n\\\\n- [x] **P0 / Creator Handoff contract is now clear, but the authoring loop still relies too much on implied escalation and loosely bundled evidence:\\\\n- `skill-creator` stops at starter drafting plus `quick_validate.py`, but does not yet leave behind one canonical durable artifact for the next stage;\\\\n- `skill-builder` already owns eval and description-optimization surfaces, but it does not yet present one first-class round model that explains how candidate and baseline runs are prepared, compared, reviewed, and promoted;\\\\n- downstream surfaces already point back to `skill-builder`, but they do not yet depend on one explicit evidence bundle and readiness-state story;\\\\n- existing report artifacts such as `result.json`, `summary.json`, `scorecard.json`, and `release_manifest.json` are useful, but they do not yet expose the specific comparative loop concepts the spec now requires.\\\\n\\\\nWithout a deliberate implementation sequence, execution will drift in one of two ways:\\\\n- the docs will describe the right lifecycle, but helper outputs and eval artifacts will still not prove it; or\\\\n- the harness will grow new fields and files ad hoc, but the family skills will still not teach the same contract to users and maintainers.\\\\n\\\\n## Requirements Trace\\\\n\\\\n- R1. existing regression suite for eval-mode and runner-shape behavior\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/release-manifest.template.json`\\\\n  - current artifact contract template for release runs\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/quality-tools.md`\\\\n  - current downstream plugin-packaging boundary and validator expectations\\\\n\\\\n### Institutional Learnings\\\\n\\\\n- Keep local packaging canonical while importing useful upstream improvements; do not let the Anthropic reference reopen local family-boundary churn.\\\\n- This repo works best when the contract is visible in both markdown and the validator or report outputs that maintainers actually use.\\\\n- For repo-focused closeout, the standard broad validation path remains preflight first and `bash Infrastructure/scripts/validation-and-linting/verify-work.sh` before completion claims.\\\\n\\\\n### External References\\\\n\\\\n- Anthropic pinned `skill-creator` at commit `98669c11ca63e9c81c11501e1437e5c47b556621`\\\\n- OpenAI and Codex guidance already incorporated into the governing spec as of 2026-04-04\\\\n\\\\n## Key Technical Decisions\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 1: Use a dedicated target-skill artifact file at `Infrastructure/references/handoff-package.md` as the phase-one `HandoffPackage` path.\\\\n  - Rationale: it is durable, repo-visible, naturally colocated with the authored skill, and distinct from chat-only summaries or repo-global plan docs.\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 2: Reuse existing machine-readable eval outputs and add only one small human-review surface when necessary.\\\\n  - Rationale: `result.json`, `summary.json`, `scorecard.json`, and `release_manifest.json` already exist. The lowest-churn upgrade is to enrich them with round-state and baseline metadata, and add `comparison_review.md` only for the qualitative side the current artifacts do not express clearly enough.\\\\n  - Phase-one ownership map:\\\\n    - `result.json`: per-case candidate-versus-baseline evidence, round state, metric availability state, and optional qualitative-review artifact pointer\\\\n    - `summary.json`: run-level rollup of readiness decisions, blocked rounds, and neutral-baseline justification references\\\\n    - `scorecard.json`: CI-facing normalized pass/fail surface that stays additive and does not become the canonical narrative record\\\\n    - `release_manifest.json`: thin release-facing snapshot that references richer report artifacts rather than duplicating every round-detail field\\\\n    - `comparison_review.md`: optional run-scoped human-readable comparison artifact under the reports directory, not a versioned skill artifact\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 3: Keep `neutral_repo_baseline` planner-approved and human-justified only.\\\\n  - Rationale: allowing the builder lane to improvise baselines would weaken the whole comparative loop.\\\\n  - Phase-one source of truth: store the human approval and justification in `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/evals.yaml`, and require run artifacts to copy or reference that record rather than inventing a parallel approval surface.\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 4: Require route and description assessment in every non-trivial round, but require edits only when the evidence shows weakness or ambiguity.\\\\n  - Rationale: this keeps the loop disciplined without forcing meaningless churn into every pass.\\\\n\\\\n- Decision 5: Treat skill-sync and catalog regeneration as part of closeout when user-facing skill descriptions or metadata change.\\\\n  - Rationale: the family is public-facing, and stale indexes would make the new contract partially invisible even if the files themselves are correct.\\\\n\\\\n## Open Questions\\\\n\\\\n### Resolved During Planning\\\\n\\\\n- What should the smallest durable creator-to-builder artifact be?\\\\n  - Resolution: `Infrastructure/references/handoff-package.md` inside the target skill.\\\\n\\\\n- Which repo-native artifact should carry comparative review evidence?\\\\n  - Resolution: enrich the existing JSON report surfaces first; add `comparison_review.md` per run only for the human-readable qualitative delta that current JSON artifacts do not already express.\\\\n\\\\n- Should route and description optimization be mandatory every round?\\\\n  - Resolution: assessment is mandatory every non-trivial round; edits are mandatory only when evidence shows trigger weakness, ambiguity, or misleading descriptions.\\\\n\\\\n### Deferred to Implementation\\\\n\\\\n- Whether `Skills/skill-creator/Infrastructure/scripts/init_skill.py` should auto-scaffold a starter `Infrastructure/references/handoff-package.md` placeholder, or whether a reference template plus `SKILL.md` guidance is sufficient for phase one.\\\\n  - Deferred because the lower-churn path should be chosen after the execution pass confirms whether deterministic scaffolding materially reduces drift.\\\\n  - Phase-one decision rule: keep this docs-and-template only unless execution shows repeated artifact omission, validator ambiguity, or enough repeated manual drift that the template is no longer a reliable contract.\\\\n\\\\n- Whether `release_manifest.json` should duplicate all new readiness-state fields, or only reference the richer `summary.json` and per-case `result.json` outputs.\\\\n  - Deferred because the existing consumers may only need a narrow additive change.\\\\n  - Phase-one decision rule: keep `release_manifest.json` thin by default and only duplicate new readiness fields when a real consumer proves the pointer-plus-summary model is insufficient.\\\\n\\\\n## recursive skill-graph contracts by adding (1) canonical lesson persistence, (2) required daily telemetry outputs, (3) run/operator control invariants (idempotency, ownership, recovery), (4) real adversarial judge paths, and (5) reviewer authorization enforcement.\\\\n\\\\n### Key opportunities\\\\n- Improve auditability and safety before Phase-4 retrieval rollout.\\\\n- Make governance automatable in CI and human review.\\\\n- Reduce uncertainty between docs and runtime behavior.\\\\n\\\\n### Chosen solution\\\\nExecute one consolidated implementation pass with a small rollout sequence:\\\\n- establish canonical registry + promotion write path,\\\\n- harden event/telemetry always-on outputs,\\\\n- enforce lock/idempotency/adversarial controls,\\\\n- strengthen reviewer checks and version CAS,\\\\n- add docs + verification updates.\\\\n\\\\n### Execution-loop and control architecture (agent-native-architecture focus)\\\\n**schema_version: 1.0**\\\\n\\\\n- **Objective:** Ensure every run is resumable, safely abortable, and auditable with deterministic completion semantics.\\\\n- **Constraints:** No silent failures, no hidden side effects, and operator control must always outrank normal loop progress.\\\\n- **Failure cost if wrong:** accidental duplicate promotions, incomplete audit trail, and unauthorized canonical graph mutation.\\\\n\\\\n#### Parity and control map (high priority paths)\\\\n| User action | Agent capability path | Current gap |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| Trigger loop run | `recursive_skill_loop.py` CLI options + run directory contracts | Partial: kill/abort behavior is currently secondary to normal terminal transitions |\\\\n| Resume/replay after interruption | run-id + resume path + deterministic journals | Partial: stale/replay duplicate handling exists but needs explicit blocked + rollback state |\\\\n| Emergency stop run | No explicit kill-switch contract | **Gap (high):** no authoritative kill behavior for incident control |\\\\n| Approve canonical lesson | `human_promote_recursive_run.sh` + validator | Needs explicit version-locked rollback semantics |\\\\n| Roll back/undo bad run mutation | Not explicitly modeled | **Gap (high):** need terminal rollback and artifact cleanup contract |\\\\n\\\\n#### Execution-loop contract additions\\\\n- **Start:** run enters `run_initialized` and must emit `run_state_changed` before any judge step.\\\\n- **Continue:** each meaningful transition must emit `run_state_changed`; loops stop only on terminal states.\\\\n- **Public contract compatibility:** existing public contract is `terminal_status \\\\u2208 {passed|failed|escalated|aborted}` and `stop_reason \\\\u2208 {pass|budget_exhausted|escalated|aborted|policy_failed|evaluator_conflict|dependency_missing}` from `docs/skill-graphs/index.md`; implementation must normalize control states through event fields (not through custom status fields):\\\\n  - `run_completed` -> `terminal_status=passed`, `stop_reason=pass`\\\\n  - `run_failed` -> `terminal_status=failed`, `stop_reason=policy_failed`\\\\n  - `run_aborted` -> `terminal_status=aborted`, `stop_reason=aborted`\\\\n  - `run_rollforward_blocked` -> `terminal_status=failed`, `stop_reason=policy_failed`, blocker event `blocker_code=run_rollforward_blocked`\\\\n  - `run_rollback_required` -> `terminal_status=failed`, `stop_reason=dependency_missing`, blocker event `blocker_code=run_rollback_required`\\\\n- **Partial completion:** non-terminal checkpoints (`run_judgment_wait`, `run_adversarial_wait`, `run_operator_approval_required`) are explicit and must persist outputs for operator handoff.\\\\n- **Blocked state behavior:** duplicate run lock, stale resume token, CAS mismatch, or reviewer-policy rejection must transition to explicit blocked/rollback states, not implicit exits.\\\\n- **Kill-switch:** add a high-priority `--kill-switch-file` (or env-equivalent) checked before/after state transitions:\\\\n  - writes `run_state_changed` reason `kill_switch_activated`\\\\n  - emits terminal event `run_aborted`\\\\n  - releases run lock and persists a rollback recommendation record.\\\\n- **Rollback:** canonical lesson writes and promotion files must include lineage so rollback/replay can be reasoned from artifacts alone (version, predecessor id, expected-version origin, and operator).\\\\n- **Migration guard:** document this mapping as an explicit contract extension with explicit removal criteria in `docs/skill-graphs/schemas/gate-contract.schema.md` before Phase-4 enablement.\\\\n\\\\n#### Rollback / recovery invariants\\\\n- **Idempotency key + state lock** must gate duplicate processing attempts.\\\\n- **Expected-version CAS** is the normal path for safe re-promote; mismatch enters `run_rollforward_blocked` and emits explicit blocker event.\\\\n- **Recovery policy:** stale terminal output retries must be no-op, while non-terminal stale resumes must fail closed into `run_rollback_required`.\\\\n- **Operator controls:** kill-switch and allowlisted approve path are highest priority control planes and must preempt normal judge flow.\\\\n\\\\n### Research Insights\\\\n\\\\n**Best practices:**\\\\n- Treat the loop as a deterministic state machine with an explicit terminal-state enum and transitions validated by schema; every non-idempotent write should be keyed by run id.\\\\n- Apply two-level concurrency model: process-level mutex first, then artifact-level optimistic lock (CAS) before any canonical mutation.\\\\n- Separate \\\\u201ccontrol plane\\\\u201d events (approval, lock, kill, rollback) from \\\\u201ccandidate outcomes\\\\u201d events to simplify audit review.\\\\n\\\\n**Performance considerations:**\\\\n- Keep state writes append-only and periodic flushes frequent; avoid locking across long judge calls.\\\\n- Pre-create lock files with atomic rename to reduce races under concurrent starts.\\\\n\\\\n**Implementation details:**\\\\n- Consider explicit transition table in JSON Schema for allowed edges, with tests for illegal transitions.\\\\n- Add an invariant that blocked/rollback states must include a human-readable blocker plus machine-readable code.\\\\n\\\\n**Edge cases:**\\\\n- Concurrent starts with same run_id should be rejected before evaluation begins.\\\\n- Kill-switch asserted during active write should force immediate flush and avoid partial mutation; prefer two-phase commit style for canonical writes.\\\\n- Replay of a completed run should never re-open approval path.\\\\n\\\\n**References:**\\\\n- Python process locking and atomic file write patterns (temp-file rename semantics)\\\\n- GitHub Actions artifact conventions and matrix-safe upload ordering\\\\n\\\\n## 1) Scope and boundaries\\\\n\\\\n### In scope\\\\n- `run_*/run.json`, `iteration_journal.jsonl`, and `promotion_decision.json` remain emitted and schema-valid.\\\\n- Canonical lesson decisions are persisted, versioned, and enforced via expected-version CAS.\\\\n- Non-allowlisted reviewers cannot approve.\\\\n- `build_recursive_skill_shadow_report.py` always produces required daily telemetry outputs.\\\\n- `--emit-debug-artifacts` only controls extra verbose artifacts, not core telemetry.\\\\n- Kill-switch activation at any checkpoint immediately transitions to terminal abort output with explicit rollback recommendation and lock release.\\\\n- Duplicate terminal transitions or stale resumes produce explicit blocked/rollback artifacts instead of silent exit.\\\\n- Blocked duplicate promotion attempt (CAS fail, lock contention, policy reject) recursive skill-graph contracts by adding (1) canonical lesson persistence, (2) required daily telemetry outputs, (3) run/operator control invariants (idempotency, ownership, recovery), (4) real adversarial judge paths, and (5) reviewer authorization enforcement.\\\\n\\\\n### Key opportunities\\\\n- Improve auditability and safety before Phase-4 retrieval rollout.\\\\n- Make governance automatable in CI and human review.\\\\n- Reduce uncertainty between docs and runtime behavior.\\\\n\\\\n### Chosen solution\\\\nExecute one consolidated implementation pass with a small rollout sequence:\\\\n- establish canonical registry + promotion write path,\\\\n- harden event/telemetry always-on outputs,\\\\n- enforce lock/idempotency/adversarial controls,\\\\n- strengthen reviewer checks and version CAS,\\\\n- add docs + verification updates.\\\\n\\\\n### Execution-loop and control architecture (agent-native-architecture focus)\\\\n**schema_version: 1.0**\\\\n\\\\n- **Objective:** Ensure every run is resumable, safely abortable, and auditable with deterministic completion semantics.\\\\n- **Constraints:** No silent failures, no hidden side effects, and operator control must always outrank normal loop progress.\\\\n- **Failure cost if wrong:** accidental duplicate promotions, incomplete audit trail, and unauthorized canonical graph mutation.\\\\n\\\\n#### Parity and control map (high priority paths)\\\\n| User action | Agent capability path | Current gap |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| Trigger loop run | `recursive_skill_loop.py` CLI options + run directory contracts | Partial: kill/abort behavior is currently secondary to normal terminal transitions |\\\\n| Resume/replay after interruption | run-id + resume path + deterministic journals | Partial: stale/replay duplicate handling exists but needs explicit blocked + rollback state |\\\\n| Emergency stop run | No explicit kill-switch contract | **Gap (high):** no authoritative kill behavior for incident control |\\\\n| Approve canonical lesson | `human_promote_recursive_run.sh` + validator | Needs explicit version-locked rollback semantics |\\\\n| Roll back/undo bad run mutation | Not explicitly modeled | **Gap (high):** need terminal rollback and artifact cleanup contract |\\\\n\\\\n#### Execution-loop contract additions\\\\n- **Start:** run enters `run_initialized` and must emit `run_state_changed` before any judge step.\\\\n- **Continue:** each meaningful transition must emit `run_state_changed`; loops stop only on terminal states.\\\\n- **Public contract compatibility:** existing public contract is `terminal_status \\\\u2208 {passed|failed|escalated|aborted}` and `stop_reason \\\\u2208 {pass|budget_exhausted|escalated|aborted|policy_failed|evaluator_conflict|dependency_missing}` from `docs/skill-graphs/index.md`; implementation must normalize control states through event fields (not through custom status fields):\\\\n  - `run_completed` -> `terminal_status=passed`, `stop_reason=pass`\\\\n  - `run_failed` -> `terminal_status=failed`, `stop_reason=policy_failed`\\\\n  - `run_aborted` -> `terminal_status=aborted`, `stop_reason=aborted`\\\\n  - `run_rollforward_blocked` -> `terminal_status=failed`, `stop_reason=policy_failed`, blocker event `blocker_code=run_rollforward_blocked`\\\\n  - `run_rollback_required` -> `terminal_status=failed`, `stop_reason=dependency_missing`, blocker event `blocker_code=run_rollback_required`\\\\n- **Partial completion:** non-terminal checkpoints (`run_judgment_wait`, `run_adversarial_wait`, `run_operator_approval_required`) are explicit and must persist outputs for operator handoff.\\\\n- **Blocked state behavior:** duplicate run lock, stale resume token, CAS mismatch, or reviewer-policy rejection must transition to explicit blocked/rollback states, not implicit exits.\\\\n- **Kill-switch:** add a high-priority `--kill-switch-file` (or env-equivalent) checked before/after state transitions:\\\\n  - writes `run_state_changed` reason `kill_switch_activated`\\\\n  - emits terminal event `run_aborted`\\\\n  - releases run lock and persists a rollback recommendation record.\\\\n- **Rollback:** canonical lesson writes and promotion files must include lineage so rollback/replay can be reasoned from artifacts alone (version, predecessor id, expected-version origin, and operator).\\\\n- **Migration guard:** document this mapping as an explicit contract extension with explicit removal criteria in `docs/skill-graphs/schemas/gate-contract.schema.md` before Phase-4 enablement.\\\\n\\\\n#### Rollback / recovery invariants\\\\n- **Idempotency key + state lock** must gate duplicate processing attempts.\\\\n- **Expected-version CAS** is the normal path for safe re-promote; mismatch enters `run_rollforward_blocked` and emits explicit blocker event.\\\\n- **Recovery policy:** stale terminal output retries must be no-op, while non-terminal stale resumes must fail closed into `run_rollback_required`.\\\\n- **Operator controls:** kill-switch and allowlisted approve path are highest priority control planes and must preempt normal judge flow.\\\\n\\\\n### Research Insights\\\\n\\\\n**Best practices:**\\\\n- Treat the loop as a deterministic state machine with an explicit terminal-state enum and transitions validated by schema; every non-idempotent write should be keyed by run id.\\\\n- Apply two-level concurrency model: process-level mutex first, then artifact-level optimistic lock (CAS) before any canonical mutation.\\\\n- Separate \\\\u201ccontrol plane\\\\u201d events (approval, lock, kill, rollback) from \\\\u201ccandidate outcomes\\\\u201d events to simplify audit review.\\\\n\\\\n**Performance considerations:**\\\\n- Keep state writes append-only and periodic flushes frequent; avoid locking across long judge calls.\\\\n- Pre-create lock files with atomic rename to reduce races under concurrent starts.\\\\n\\\\n**Implementation details:**\\\\n- Consider explicit transition table in JSON Schema for allowed edges, with tests for illegal transitions.\\\\n- Add an invariant that blocked/rollback states must include a human-readable blocker plus machine-readable code.\\\\n\\\\n**Edge cases:**\\\\n- Concurrent starts with same run_id should be rejected before evaluation begins.\\\\n- Kill-switch asserted during active write should force immediate flush and avoid partial mutation; prefer two-phase commit style for canonical writes.\\\\n- Replay of a completed run should never re-open approval path.\\\\n\\\\n**References:**\\\\n- Python process locking and atomic file write patterns (temp-file rename semantics)\\\\n- GitHub Actions artifact conventions and matrix-safe upload ordering\\\\n\\\\n## 1) Scope and boundaries\\\\n\\\\n### In scope\\\\n- thresholds.\\\\n\\\\n**Validation additions:**\\\\n- Add assertions for telemetry file presence in both normal and failure mode.\\\\n- Add fixture-driven checks for `run_state_changed` transitions, \\\"# Harness Engineering Plan Doctrine\\\\n\\\\nThis retained doctrine preserves the context used to harden `he-plan` without loading it into every invocation.\\\\n\\\\n## Sources Synthesized\\\\n\\\\n- `SKILL (14).md`: universal planning workflow, source handling, synthesis, depth, local/external research, plan template, confidence checks, and handoff.\\\\n- `universal-planning.md`: non-software planning classification, research need, domain-appropriate plan shape, and save/share handling.\\\\n- `synthesis-summary (1).md`: Stated/Inferred/Out-of-scope checkpoint, headless assumptions routing, and complete-replacement revision discipline.\\\\n- `plan-handoff.md`: mandatory document review after confidence checks, final options, tracker handoff, and stale-review handling.\\\\n- `deepening-workflow.md`: confidence-gap scoring, targeted reviewer dispatch, direct vs artifact-backed research, and accepted-finding integration.\\\\n- `visual-communication (1).md`: dependency graphs, interaction diagrams, comparison tables, and visual anti-patterns.\\\\n- `testing-anti-patterns.md`: real-behavior tests, mock discipline, complete mocks, and no test-only production methods.\\\\n- `SKILL (12).md` and `SKILL (13).md`: useful TDD and execution-handoff ideas, adapted away from micro-step code plans.\\\\n- `plan-document-reviewer-prompt.md`: implementation-readiness review rubric.\\\\n- Live `/Users/jamiecraik/dev/codex` and codex-repo MCP: Codex Plan Mode behavior, `update_plan` distinction, `request_user_input` semantics, proposed-plan rendering, and implementation confirmation flow.\\\\n\\\\n## Transferable Codex Plan Mode Lessons\\\\n\\\\nPlan Mode works because it separates exploration, intent, and implementation shape:\\\\n\\\\n1. Ground in the environment first. Discover repo facts, patterns, configs, and schemas before asking.\\\\n2. Ask only when the answer changes scope, architecture, sequencing, risk, or an assumption.\\\\n3. Treat discoverable facts and preferences differently.\\\\n4. Avoid mutation while planning. Planning may inspect, search, and run non-mutating checks, but implementation belongs elsewhere.\\\\n5. Keep `update_plan` separate from plan mode. It is a live checklist/progress tool, not the durable plan artifact.\\\\n6. Final plans should be complete replacement artifacts. Partial deltas are easy for downstream agents to misapply.\\\\n\\\\nCodex chat uses `<proposed_plan>` to render approved plan text and can offer \\\\\\\"implement this plan\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"clear context and implement\\\\\\\" actions. Harness Engineering should not require that wrapper inside saved plan files, but it should preserve the underlying behavior: clear handoff, complete artifact, and a fresh-context implementation option when context pressure is high.\\\\n\\\\n## HE Plan Shape\\\\n\\\\nA Harness Engineering plan is ready when another agent can implement it without making product or architecture decisions. It should include:\\\\n\\\\n- problem frame and scope boundary\\\\n- source traceability to Linear/spec/requirements/brainstorm/UI criteria\\\\n- stable unit IDs and stable acceptance IDs\\\\n- dependencies and blocker order\\\\n- repo-relative file paths\\\\n- test file paths and concrete scenarios\\\\n- validation outcomes, rollout notes, rollback notes, and residual risks\\\\n- Linear/spec/plan/PR evidence matrix for tracked work\\\\n\\\\nThe plan should not include copy-paste implementation code, exact shell choreography, commit commands, or RED/GREEN/REFACTOR micro-steps. It may include directional sketches, diagrams, or pseudocode when they help reviewers validate shape, but those must be explicitly non-prescriptive.\\\\n\\\\n## Source Resolution\\\\n\\\\nPrefer the strongest source in this order:\\\\n\\\\n1. Existing plan path or obvious current plan to resume.\\\\n2. Active Linear issue and related parent/child/blocking issue graph.\\\\n3. Requirements or brainstorm document with acceptance examples and scope boundaries.\\\\n4. Approved spec or UI spec.\\\\n5. Direct feature, bug, refactor, or improvement description.\\\\n\\\\nIf the source has unresolved product blockers, route back to `he-brainstorm` or `he-spec`. If the source has technical questions that planning can resolve through repo or docs research, resolve them during planning. If the answer depends on writing code, running changed behavior, or seeing test failures, record it as a deferred implementation note.\\\\n\\\\n## Depth And Research\\\\n\\\\nUse the smallest depth that protects delivery:\\\\n\\\\n- Lightweight: compact plan, low ambiguity, straight-line dependencies.\\\\n- Standard: normal feature/refactor/bug with meaningful decisions and validation.\\\\n- Deep: cross-cutting, risky, ambiguous, migration/security/privacy/payment/external API work, or work touching external contract surfaces.\\\\n\\\\nLocal research always comes first. External research is warranted for high-risk domains, third-party APIs, missing local patterns, current framework behavior, or unfamiliar territory. Skip external research when local patterns are strong, recent, and directly applicable.\\\\n\\\\nReclassify lightweight work to standard when it touches environment variables, public APIs, CLI flags, CI, shared types, or externally consumed docs.\\\\n\\\\n## Synthesis And Assumptions\\\\n\\\\nUse Stated, Inferred, and Out-of-scope checkpoints when the agent has made consequential assumptions. In interactive work, revise and re-present after user changes until explicitly confirmed. In headless work, put unconfirmed Inferred bets in `## Assumptions` so reviewers and `he-work` can scrutinize them.\\\\n\\\\n## Deepening\\\\n\\\\nDeepen only where confidence gaps are real. \\\"he-plan-doctrine.md\\\", \\\"structuredContent\\\": {\\\"title\\\": \\\"he-plan-doctrine.md\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# Harness Engineering Plan Doctrine\\\\n\\\\nThis retained doctrine preserves the context used to harden `he-plan` without loading it into every invocation.\\\\n\\\\n## Sources Synthesized\\\\n\\\\n- `SKILL (14).md`: universal planning workflow, source handling, synthesis, depth, local/external research, plan template, confidence checks, and handoff.\\\\n- `universal-planning.md`: non-software planning classification, research need, domain-appropriate plan shape, and save/share handling.\\\\n- `synthesis-summary (1).md`: Stated/Inferred/Out-of-scope checkpoint, headless assumptions routing, and complete-replacement revision discipline.\\\\n- `plan-handoff.md`: mandatory document review after confidence checks, final options, tracker handoff, and stale-review handling.\\\\n- `deepening-workflow.md`: confidence-gap scoring, targeted reviewer dispatch, direct vs artifact-backed research, and accepted-finding integration.\\\\n- `visual-communication (1).md`: dependency graphs, interaction diagrams, comparison tables, and visual anti-patterns.\\\\n- `testing-anti-patterns.md`: real-behavior tests, mock discipline, complete mocks, and no test-only production methods.\\\\n- `SKILL (12).md` and `SKILL (13).md`: useful TDD and execution-handoff ideas, adapted away from micro-step code plans.\\\\n- `plan-document-reviewer-prompt.md`: implementation-readiness review rubric.\\\\n- Live `/Users/jamiecraik/dev/codex` and codex-repo MCP: Codex Plan Mode behavior, `update_plan` distinction, `request_user_input` semantics, proposed-plan rendering, and implementation confirmation flow.\\\\n\\\\n## Transferable Codex Plan Mode Lessons\\\\n\\\\nPlan Mode works because it separates exploration, intent, and implementation shape:\\\\n\\\\n1. Ground in the environment first. Discover repo facts, patterns, configs, and schemas before asking.\\\\n2. Ask only when the answer changes scope, architecture, sequencing, risk, or an assumption.\\\\n3. Treat discoverable facts and preferences differently.\\\\n4. Avoid mutation while planning. Planning may inspect, search, and run non-mutating checks, but implementation belongs elsewhere.\\\\n5. Keep `update_plan` separate from plan mode. It is a live checklist/progress tool, not the durable plan artifact.\\\\n6. Final plans should be complete replacement artifacts. Partial deltas are easy for downstream agents to misapply.\\\\n\\\\nCodex chat uses `<proposed_plan>` to render approved plan text and can offer \\\\\\\"implement this plan\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"clear context and implement\\\\\\\" actions. Harness Engineering should not require that wrapper inside saved plan files, but it should preserve the underlying behavior: clear handoff, complete artifact, and a fresh-context implementation option when context pressure is high.\\\\n\\\\n## HE Plan Shape\\\\n\\\\nA Harness Engineering plan is ready when another agent can implement it without making product or architecture decisions. It should include:\\\\n\\\\n- problem frame and scope boundary\\\\n- source traceability to Linear/spec/requirements/brainstorm/UI criteria\\\\n- stable unit IDs and stable acceptance IDs\\\\n- dependencies and blocker order\\\\n- repo-relative file paths\\\\n- test file paths and concrete scenarios\\\\n- validation outcomes, rollout notes, rollback notes, and residual risks\\\\n- Linear/spec/plan/PR evidence matrix for tracked work\\\\n\\\\nThe plan should not include copy-paste implementation code, exact shell choreography, commit commands, or RED/GREEN/REFACTOR micro-steps. It may include directional sketches, diagrams, or pseudocode when they help reviewers validate shape, but those must be explicitly non-prescriptive.\\\\n\\\\n## Source Resolution\\\\n\\\\nPrefer the strongest source in this order:\\\\n\\\\n1. Existing plan path or obvious current plan to resume.\\\\n2. Active Linear issue and related parent/child/blocking issue graph.\\\\n3. Requirements or brainstorm document with acceptance examples and scope boundaries.\\\\n4. Approved spec or UI spec.\\\\n5. Direct feature, bug, refactor, or improvement description.\\\\n\\\\nIf the source has unresolved product blockers, route back to `he-brainstorm` or `he-spec`. If the source has technical questions that planning can resolve through repo or docs research, resolve them during planning. If the answer depends on writing code, running changed behavior, or seeing test failures, record it as a deferred implementation note.\\\\n\\\\n## Depth And Research\\\\n\\\\nUse the smallest depth that protects delivery:\\\\n\\\\n- Lightweight: compact plan, low ambiguity, straight-line dependencies.\\\\n- Standard: normal feature/refactor/bug with meaningful decisions and validation.\\\\n- Deep: cross-cutting, risky, ambiguous, migration/security/privacy/payment/external API work, or work touching external contract surfaces.\\\\n\\\\nLocal research always comes first. External research is warranted for high-risk domains, third-party APIs, missing local patterns, current framework behavior, or unfamiliar territory. Skip external research when local patterns are strong, recent, and directly applicable.\\\\n\\\\nReclassify lightweight work to standard when it touches environment variables, public APIs, CLI flags, CI, shared types, or externally consumed docs.\\\\n\\\\n## Synthesis And Assumptions\\\\n\\\\nUse Stated, Inferred, and Out-of-scope checkpoints when the agent has made consequential assumptions. In interactive work, revise and re-present after user changes until explicitly confirmed. In headless work, put unconfirmed Inferred bets in `## Assumptions` so reviewers and `he-work` can scrutinize them.\\\\n\\\\n## Deepening\\\\n\\\\nDeepen only where confidence gaps are real. Score sections by missing rationale, weak source grounding, vague units, bad sequencing, shallow tests, hidden blockers, weak rollout, and missing system impact. Dispatch targeted reviewers only for the section/risk being strengthened.\\\\n\\\\nDeepening should make the plan stronger, not longer.\\\\n\\\\n## Testing Guidance\\\\n\\\\nPlans must require real behavior tests. Avoid test scenarios that only assert mocks, snapshots of mocked children, or implementation internals. Include happy path, edge case, error path, and integration scenarios only where they genuinely apply.\\\\n\\\\nFor non-feature units, use an explicit no-test rationale rather than leaving tests blank.\\\\n\\\\n## Visual Guidance\\\\n\\\\nUse visuals when they reduce reader work:\\\\n\\\\n- dependency graph for non-linear unit dependencies\\\\n- interaction diagram for three or more affected surfaces\\\\n- comparison table for modes, variants, or alternatives\\\\n- state diagram for state-heavy lifecycle\\\\n\\\\nSkip visuals that duplicate prose or smuggle implementation detail into the plan.\\\\n\\\\n## Handoff\\\\n\\\\nAfter the plan is complete, hand off to:\\\\n\\\\n- `he-work` for implementation\\\\n- Linear workflow when creating or updating tracked work\\\\n- `he-deepen-plan` or document review when confidence gaps remain\\\\n\\\\nDo not auto-implement from `he-plan`. The handoff can recommend the next workflow, but the planning skill itself remains plan-only.\\\\n\\\", \\\"display_url\\\": sequencing, blocker classification, and closeout verification\\\\n\\\\n- Added an explicit artifact-ownership matrix so `ce-work` can land the builder and harness changes without re-deciding where blocker-control gates so compatibility regressions, runner noise, and partial-rollout drift are classified consistently before closeout.\\\\n\\\\n## Overview\\\\n\\\\nUpgrade the skill-authoring family from a clean routing split into a coherent, evidence-backed authoring loop without undoing the lifecycle boundaries that were just stabilized.\\\\n\\\\nThis plan implements the approved spec by:\\\\n- making `skill-creator` produce a durable creator-to-builder handoff artifact for non-trivial skills;\\\\n- teaching `skill-builder` one explicit comparative iteration loop with frozen inputs, baseline rules, round states, and visible review evidence;\\\\n- keeping `skill-installer` and `plugin-builder` as downstream-only owners gated by `ContractValidityEvidence`;\\\\n- extending existing repo-native eval and reporting surfaces instead of introducing a new standalone viewer or parallel harness.\\\\n\\\\nPlan mode: `standard-plan`  \\\\nPlan depth: `deep`  \\\\nExecution posture: artifact-contract-first, then builder evidence surfaces, then eval enforcement, then downstream gating and full-family validation.\\\\n\\\\n## Problem Frame\\\\n\\\\nThe family routing contract is now clear, but the authoring loop still relies too much on implied escalation and loosely bundled evidence:\\\\n- `skill-creator` stops at starter drafting plus `quick_validate.py`, but does not yet leave behind one canonical durable artifact for the next stage;\\\\n- `skill-builder` already owns eval and description-optimization surfaces, but it does not yet present one first-class round model that explains how candidate and baseline runs are prepared, compared, reviewed, and promoted;\\\\n- downstream surfaces already point back to `skill-builder`, but they do not yet depend on one explicit evidence bundle and readiness-state story;\\\\n- existing report artifacts such as `result.json`, `summary.json`, `scorecard.json`, and `release_manifest.json` are useful, but they do not yet expose the specific comparative loop concepts the spec now requires.\\\\n\\\\nWithout a deliberate implementation sequence, execution will drift in one of two ways:\\\\n- the docs will describe the right lifecycle, but helper outputs and eval artifacts will still not prove it; or\\\\n- the harness will grow new fields and files ad hoc, but the family skills will still not teach the same contract to users and maintainers.\\\\n\\\\n## Requirements Trace\\\\n\\\\n- R1. Preserve the current family split and routing ownership across `skill-creator`, `skill-builder`, `skill-installer`, and `plugin-builder`.\\\\n  Trace: spec goals 1 and 7; `SA1`\\\\n- R2. Non-trivial creator-stage work must end with a durable dedicated handoff artifact file carrying the required context fields.\\\\n  Trace: spec `HandoffPackage`; spec invariants; `SA2`, `SA2a`, `SA3`\\\\n- R3. `skill-builder` must expose one explicit non-trivial iteration loop with prompt preparation, baseline selection, frozen comparison inputs, evidence capture, tuning assessment, and round decision.\\\\n  Trace: spec `IterationRound`, `ComparisonInputs`, `IterationRoundState`; `SA4`, `SA5`, `SA7`, `SA14`, `SA15`\\\\n- R4. Comparative evidence must preserve both machine-readable and human-reviewable signals, including metric unavailability and readiness-state distinctions.\\\\n  Trace: spec `EvalEvidenceBundle`; failure model; observability; `SA6`, `SA17`\\\\n- R5. Install and plugin packaging surfaces must remain downstream-only and require `ContractValidityEvidence`.\\\\n  Trace: spec downstream handoff rules; `SA9`, `SA10`, `SA18`\\\\n- R6. The implementation must stay repo-native by extending existing docs, eval manifests, and report artifacts instead of introducing a new viewer or cloned upstream workspace.\\\\n  Trace: spec goals 8 and non-goals; `SA11`, `SA12`, `SA13`\\\\n\\\\n## Scope Boundaries\\\\n\\\\nIn scope:\\\\n- authoring-family skill docs and metadata:\\\\n  - `Skills/skill-creator/`\\\\n  - `Skills/skill-builder/`\\\\n  - `Skills/skill-installer/`\\\\n  - `Skills/plugin-builder/`\\\\n- creator-stage artifact guidance and reusable template support\\\\n- `skill-builder` iteration, evidence, and reporting contract\\\\n- eval harness additions required to protect the new loop\\\\n- downstream handoff wording and readiness gating\\\\n- repo validation and sync work needed to keep public skill surfaces aligned\\\\n\\\\nOut of scope:\\\\n- merging or renaming the family\\\\n- a repo-wide skill-evals platform redesign\\\\n- a new dedicated UI artifact or UI plan\\\\n- a new standalone viewer application for eval review\\\\n- policy changes that would make `skill-builder` explicit-only\\\\n- runtime router changes outside the named family surfaces and existing eval/reporting helpers\\\\n\\\\n## Context and Research\\\\n\\\\n### Relevant Code and Patterns\\\\n\\\\n- `Docs/specs/2026-04-03-feat-skill-authoring-family-contract-spec.md`\\\\n  - existing deterministic scaffolding surface if template emission or signposting needs automation\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/SKILL.md`\\\\n  - current lifecycle-maintenance contract with smoke/release eval and description-optimization references\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/iteration-and-testing.md`\\\\n  - likely home for the explicit round model if `SKILL.md` needs slimmer routing-level guidance\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/description-optimization.md`\\\\n  - existing route/description improvement guidance that can become one named step in the new round\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/evals.yaml`\\\\n  - current regression suite already covering routing and packaging boundaries\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/scripts/run_skill_evals.py`\\\\n  - current machine-readable report surface writing `result.json`, `summary.json`, `scorecard.json`, `release_manifest.json`, and `junit.xml`\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/scripts/test_run_skill_evals.py`\\\\n  - existing regression suite for eval-mode and runner-shape behavior\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/release-manifest.template.json`\\\\n  - current artifact contract template for release runs\\\\n- `Skills/skill-builder/Infrastructure/references/quality-tools.md`\\\\n  -
